banner.title: promtail
banner.tagline: Tails every container log on every node, labels it with pod, node and Ceph daemon identity, and pushes it to Loki.

art.about: how container log files become labelled log batches in Loki
art.title: How promtail ships logs to Loki

explainer.title: From a log file to a labelled stream

steps.title: Discover
steps.text: The DaemonSet runs on every node, tolerating the PreferNoSchedule dedicated taint on talos-3. It tails each pod's log file on its node.
steps.scene: a small agent on each server rack

steps.title: Parse
steps.text: The CRI stage reads timestamps and streams. Relabels add the node, the namespace and, for rook-ceph, the daemon type and ID.
steps.scene: log lines sorted into three plain coloured trays, no text or labels on the trays

steps.title: Batch
steps.text: A batch flushes after 1 s or 1 MiB. Failed pushes back off from 500 ms to 5 min, for up to 10 retries.
steps.scene: crates of log lines on a conveyor belt

steps.title: Push
steps.text: Pushes to loki-headless on port 3100 with an empty tenant ID, because Loki runs with auth disabled.
steps.scene: a data packet travelling to a stacked database

steps.title: Watch
steps.text: Its own metrics feed two alerts: more than 10% request errors, and files with more than 1 GB unread.
steps.scene: a meter needle beside a warning light
